question: What is the primary focus of nursing unit management?

options.B: Balancing clinical care with administrative oversight

explanation: Unit management requires combining direct patient care skills with organizational and administrative duties. [learn more](GST321_U6_T2#GST321_U6_T2_h1)

question: Effective nursing unit management directly influences which of the following outcomes?

options.D: Patient recovery times and staff retention

explanation: Proper coordination within a ward improves both how fast patients heal and how long nurses stay on the job. [learn more](GST321_U6_T2#GST321_U6_T2_h1)

question: Conducting regular evaluations for junior nurses falls under which administrative duty?
explanation: Appraisals help managers assess staff work quality and encourage professional development. [learn more](GST321_U6_T2#GST321_U6_T2_h2)

question: Why must unit managers actively mediate disputes between staff members?

options.A: To reduce the hospital electricity bill
options.C: To replace human resource departments entirely
options.D: To preserve a harmonious working atmosphere

explanation: Resolving conflicts early prevents a toxic environment and protects teamwork on the ward. [learn more](GST321_U6_T2#GST321_U6_T2_h2)

question: Tracking hospital-acquired infections is a key component of which nursing responsibility?
explanation: Quality assurance activities monitor clinical outcomes like infection rates to maintain high care standards. [learn more](GST321_U6_T2#GST321_U6_T2_h3)

question: A ward manager assigns high-acuity patients to more experienced nurses. What is the goal of this action?

options.B: Reducing the total number of hospital beds
options.C: Matching staff skills to patient needs safely
options.D: Punishing junior nurses with extra paperwork

explanation: Acuity-based assignments ensure patients receive the level of expertise their condition demands. [learn more](GST321_U6_T2#GST321_U6_T2_h3)

question: What is a primary goal of creating fair duty rosters in a nursing unit?

options.A: Maximizing overtime pay for all workers
options.B: Preventing staff burnout and ensuring coverage
options.C: Reducing the total number of employed nurses
options.D: Eliminating the need for night shifts

explanation: Balanced scheduling keeps nurses rested and guarantees the ward is always staffed. [learn more](GST321_U6_T2#GST321_U6_T2_h4)

question: Why should a unit manager advocate for adequate staffing levels with upper management?

options.A: Extra staff automatically lowers patient hospital bills
options.B: Nurses refuse to work without financial bonuses
options.C: Adequate staffing reduces medical errors and raises morale
options.D: Hospital directors require daily reports on staff attendance

explanation: Fewer mistakes happen and nurses feel supported when there are enough hands on deck. [learn more](GST321_U6_T2#GST321_U6_T2_h4)

question: What does budgetary control in a nursing unit mainly involve?

options.A: Paying the salaries of all hospital doctors
options.C: Forecasting needs and preventing supply stockouts

explanation: Managers must track inventory to ensure life-saving supplies do not run out unexpectedly. [learn more](GST321_U6_T2#GST321_U6_T2_h5)

question: Why is resource monitoring especially critical in Nigerian healthcare units?

options.A: Government regulations forbid storing extra medicines
options.B: Resources are often scarce and waste must be minimized
options.C: Consumables never expire or get misplaced
options.D: Hospitals have unlimited funds for medical supplies

explanation: Careful tracking prevents shortages in environments where supplies are limited. [learn more](GST321_U6_T2#GST321_U6_T2_h5)

question: Which activity is part of maintaining a safe physical ward environment?

options.B: Ordering meals from external catering services
options.C: Writing the annual hospital financial report
options.D: Conducting regular safety audits for hazards

explanation: Routine checks catch hazards like broken equipment or wet floors before accidents happen. [learn more](GST321_U6_T2#GST321_U6_T2_h6)

question: Proper biomedical waste segregation on a ward primarily helps with what?

options.B: Lowering the cost of hospital electricity bills
options.D: Controlling infections and protecting public health

explanation: Sorting waste correctly stops the spread of dangerous germs and protects handlers. [learn more](GST321_U6_T2#GST321_U6_T2_h6)

question: Structured handovers and multidisciplinary rounds are examples of what?
explanation: These methods keep all members of the healthcare team updated on patient status. [learn more](GST321_U6_T2#GST321_U6_T2_h7)

question: What is the main danger of poor communication among different healthcare professionals?

options.A: Reduced need for nursing shift handovers
options.D: Faster processing of patient discharge files

explanation: When team members do not share information clearly, patient safety is compromised. [learn more](GST321_U6_T2#GST321_U6_T2_h7)

question: Which of the following is a common operational challenge in Nigerian healthcare units?

options.A: An overabundance of specialized nursing staff
options.B: Erratic water supply and frequent power outages
options.C: Excessive surplus of modern medical equipment
options.D: Immediate payment of all patient hospital bills

explanation: Infrastructure challenges like electricity and water issues are common hurdles for local managers. [learn more](GST321_U6_T2#GST321_U6_T2_h8)

question: How do resilient nurse managers handle systemic constraints in resource-limited settings?

options.A: By closing the hospital ward until funding arrives
options.B: By ignoring safety protocols to save time
options.C: By refusing to admit new patients to the facility
options.D: By optimizing local resources and maintaining staff morale

explanation: Adaptive strategies help managers keep services running despite difficult working conditions. [learn more](GST321_U6_T2#GST321_U6_T2_h8)
